why: PROMOTE. Facts (each one is a claim below, verified against the raw request log): (1) Neither version returned a single 5xx and no request on either version returned a non-200 status: canary 0/2411, stable 0/7374. (2) Overall latency is not worse on the canary: canary overall p95 is not more than 2 ms above stable overall p95 (93 vs 94 in my calculation). (3) Checkout, the revenue path, is unchanged: canary /checkout p95 is within 2 ms of stable /checkout p95. (4) The only visible difference is the /browse tail: 13 of 1200 canary /browse requests exceeded 40 ms versus 15 of 3672 stable requests, which is what lifts canary /browse p99 to 77 ms while stable sits at 28 ms. (5) Those slow /browse requests are bounded and not a developing trend: the slowest /browse request is 87 ms on BOTH versions, and the canary's slow requests occur in all four 30 s windows rather than clustering at the end of the test. Judgement: a tail that tops out at 87 ms on a page whose p50 is 22 ms is not customer-visible harm, there is no error-rate or saturation signal to go with it, and 13 events on a single pod over 120 s is within noise, so this does not justify blocking the release. Judgement: promote, but watch /browse p99 for the first 30 minutes at 100% traffic, since 4x the traffic on this code path is the one thing this canary did not test.

claims.query: function P(a,q){var s=a.slice().sort(function(x,y){return x-y;});return s[Math.min(s.length-1,Math.ceil(q/100*s.length)-1)];} function ms(rs,p){return rs.filter(function(r){return r.path===p;}).map(function(r){return r.ms;});} var cp=P(ms(canary,'/checkout'),95); var sp=P(ms(stable,'/checkout'),95); print('checkout p95 canary='+cp+' stable='+sp+' checkoutP95Within2ms='+(Math.abs(cp-sp)<=2));

claims.claim: The canary has proportionally more slow /browse requests: 13 of 1200 canary /browse requests exceeded 40 ms versus 15 of 3672 stable /browse requests, and this is what raises canary /browse p99 to 77 ms against stable 28 ms.
